published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE (see source.via). The tree's own wording, fewsterteo.py:62-67: 'The massless radial equation on -F dt^2 + dr^2/F + r^2 dOmega^2 has regular singular points at r = 0 and r = 2M and an IRREGULAR one at infinity (Q -> omega^2 != 0): the confluent Heun class, with no closed form in named special functions. For M < 0 the second regular point sits at r = 2M < 0, off the domain, and the class is unchanged. A property of the equation, derived here by sympy.' Recalled (not read) textbook content, stated only as the target of the re-derivation: the confluent Heun equation is w'' + (gamma/z + delta/(z-1) + epsilon) w' + (alpha z - q)/(z(z-1)) w = 0, two regular singular points z = 0, 1 and an irregular singular point of rank 1 at infinity, obtained by confluence from the general Heun equation.
published_hypotheses: (recalled, not read) an equation is in the confluent Heun class iff, after a Moebius map and an s-homotopic gauge, it has exactly two regular singular points and one irregular singular point of Poincare rank 1
(recalled, not read) generic parameters: confluent Heun functions do not reduce to hypergeometric-class functions; special parameter sets (polynomial/terminating cases, degenerations) do
(tree) F = 1 - 2M/r with CONSTANT M; massless, minimally coupled; separated phi = R(r) Y_lm e^{-i w t}; omega != 0 (named via 'Q -> omega^2 != 0')

The board's own device has M_ADM = 0 EXACTLY (concentric.py:3, :49), so the region outside the shell tends to precisely this closed-form case.

Moot on the device (m(0) = 0 removes r = 0 from the Schwarzschild segment), but unnamed in the sentence.

UNCOMPUTED CLAUSE, as the canonical entry already notes: 'no closed form in named special functions' carries no status at fewsterteo.py:65 and nothing at :432-452 tests it. Wording discrepancy (not an error): the confluent Heun function is itself a named special function (DLMF Sec. 31.12, Maple HeunC -- recalled, not read); the defensible reading is 'no reduction to hypergeometric-class or elementary functions for generic parameters'.

rederivation.outcome: ALL COMPUTED ROWS AS EXPECTED. C1: P = 2(r-M)/(r(r-2M)), Q = (omega^2 r^3 - l(l+1)(r-2M))/(r(r-2M)^2); finite singular points exactly {0, 2M}; r = 0 regular with indicial rho^2 (double root -> logarithmic, non-apparent); r = 2M exponents +-2iM omega; at oo r P -> 2 but r^2 Q -> oo (irregular), formal solutions e^{+-i omega r} r^{-1 +- 2iM omega} (Poincare rank 1). C2: with z = r/2M, R = e^{i omega r}(r-2M)^{2iM omega} W(z), W obeys W'' + (1/z + (1+4iM omega)/(z-1) + 4iM omega) W' + (4iM omega z - l(l+1))/(z(z-1)) W = 0 -- exactly the confluent Heun shape with gamma = 1, delta = 1 + 4iM omega, epsilon = 4iM omega, alpha = 4iM omega, q = l(l+1). The singular-point classification and the confluent-Heun membership AGREE with the tree (and with the tree's own selftest rows (e), which pass). C3: M = 0 -> spherical Bessel j_l, y_l solve it; omega = 0 -> Legendre P_l, Q_l of r/M - 1 solve it (l = 0..3, residual 0): both closed forms, both excluded only by hypotheses the tree does not state fully. C4 (Kovacic, normalised y'' = S y): poles of order 2 at 0 (1+4b = 0) and 2M (1+4b = -16M^2 omega^2), ord_oo S = 0 -> case 3 excluded; case 2 degree bound d = -2 -> excluded; case 1 candidate degrees {-1, -1, -1 +- 4iM omega} -> none a non-negative integer for real omega != 0, M != 0, any l -> NO LIOUVILLIAN SOLUTION (a polynomial-type solution is possible only at omega = -i(n+1)/(4M), purely imaginary); brute-force ansatz e^{+-i omega r}(r-2M)^{+-2iM omega} p(r), deg p <= 6, l = 0..3, M = 1, omega = 3/7: only the zero solution. C5: two non-apparent regular singular points vs one for the Kummer/Whittaker class -> no reduction to 1F1/Bessel/Whittaker by affine map + exponential/power gauge. NOT decided: equivalence through first-order operators, integral or series representations (Leaver/MST type) -- 'closed form in named special functions' is not a decidable predicate. C6: M < 0, r = 0 limit-circle (both 1 and log r in L^2(r^2/F dr) near 0). C7: Frobenius series (40 terms) about r = 2M vs mpmath odefun, M = 1, omega = 0.5, l = 1, r = 2.5 -> 2.9: relative difference 1.76e-16 -- mode functions are computable. C8: concentric.py's Plummer-core Phi gives non-rational Q; its M_ADM = 0 exterior Phi falls as 1/r^3 (no 1/r tail).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: this is a data-free mathematical classification -- its conclusion depends on no measured number, so no datum the original authors lacked can move it. Evidence: the singular-point structure, the Heun parameters (gamma = 1, delta = 1 + 4iM omega, epsilon = alpha = 4iM omega, q = l(l+1)) and the Kovacic exclusion (C4) hold for every real omega != 0 and M != 0 symbolically. What moves the tree's CONCLUSION is not external data but the board's own inputs: which metric the corridor is (M_ADM = 0 exterior -> closed-form spherical Bessel; regular core m(0) = 0 -> r = 0 not a Schwarzschild point; Plummer Phi -> non-rational coefficients), and the step from 'confluent Heun' to 'cannot be determined', which the computation (C7) contradicts. So M's suspicion is not borne out for the external result; it is borne out in the transfer to the tree -- an inaccuracy of application, not of the outside mathematics.
grade_evidence: The classification itself RE-DERIVES exactly (C1, C2; the tree's own selftest rows (e) also pass) and the 'no closed form' clause is SUPPORTED on the class the computation reaches: no Liouvillian solution for real omega != 0, M != 0 (Kovacic cases 1-3 excluded, brute force null) and no reduction to the confluent hypergeometric class by affine map + gauge (C5). It is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than it holds on and draws a stronger conclusion than it supports: (i) M != 0 is required and dropped -- at M = 0 there is a closed form (C3), and the board's device has M_ADM = 0 (concentric.py:3,49); (ii) it holds for the constant-M vacuum segment only, not for the corridor's regular-centre metric with m(r), Phi(r) (certify.py:116, fewsterteo.py:101; C8); (iii) fewsterteo.py:107 'cannot be [determined]' does not follow -- the mode functions are computable (C7, 1.76e-16); (iv) for M < 0 on (0, oo) a boundary condition at r = 0 is needed (limit-circle, C6); (v) the no-closed-form clause is uncomputed in the tree and, as worded, is not decidable ('named special functions' includes HeunC itself). No misprint or refutation of the external result is claimed. Source NAMED-NOT-READ this session (quota/egress), so the grade rests on computation, not on reading.
